result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers leave desktop at 72px and give a 390px phone a headline of roughly 35-39px. Both keep tight leading and negative tracking, leave .lead at 18px/1.5, and should wrap to about three lines. B's single clamp() scales smoothly all the way up to 72px at about 800px. A jumps from 44px to 72px at 601px, so small tablets and landscape phones can still get the cramped one-or-two-words-per-line problem. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers meet every rubric item. At 390px, A computes to 36px and B to 39px; both keep tight leading and negative tracking, leave .lead at 18px, and should wrap to about 3 lines without overflow. A edges ahead because its global clamp() scales smoothly up to 72px at about 800px. B jumps from 44px to 72px at the 601px breakpoint, which is awkward on small tablets, though B adds a useful overflow-wrap safeguard and is open that it hasn't been rendered.
